summary.name: 3D Diorama (Digital and 3D Aesthetics). The label was normalized from source descriptions, which explicitly name a 3D diorama.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: a complete miniature stage with deliberate boundaries and consistent scales for architecture, characters and props. It is seen from a clear elevated or oblique view with limited depth of field, so local actions and environmental detail read clearly. Key models and paths must stay sharp.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: compatibility lists name 3D Diorama for exploded reveals, dollies, cursor orbits, lighting-state progression and 360° orbits. Inferred: bounded explainers, campaigns, product scenes and miniature world tours fit well. Interactive HTML is suggested only as a scrubbable orbit with keyboard controls or clickable zones.
summary.limitations: Explicit: a true orbit needs finished geometry on every side. A single flat image or photo cannot support one; a labelled partial arc is the only fallback. Strict isometric, flat poster or frontal symmetric framing excludes camera orbits. Soft shadows do not establish photorealism. Source review covered only sampled seconds 1–8, with no verified motion, audio or later scenes.
summary.palette: Explicit: no exact or approved palette was supplied, and background_policy is scene_dependent. Choose the surround from subject, lighting and mood, not the cream example #EEE6D4. Example tokens #35433C, #7B9173 and #B3885F are unapproved suggestions. Reference lesson: matte, desaturated material colors, one saturated focal surface and high-contrast labels. The foreground/background pair measures 8.371:1, but both accent pairs fail 4.5:1 for body text.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: nine optional references are motion-009 parallax, 010 angle-linked orbit, 012 chapter transition, 015 storytelling, 017 exploded reveal, 019 dolly, 021 cursor orbit, 042 lighting states and 043 360° orbit. Each is used only if the scene supports its defining action. Motion-043 needs a stationary hero and camera-only movement. Video uses composition time only, with no live pointer, scroll or OrbitControls. Movement should be smooth where helpful and keep sharp cuts and reading holds.
summary.audio: Explicit: the style defines no mandatory audio. Inferred: silence, soft ambience or a restrained musical accent suits explainers, with narration taking priority over effects. Avoid a sound for every move. No audio was verified in source review, and no beat or speech timing exists. Claim music sync only with measured data, and keep any speech intelligible.
summary.assetRequirements: Explicit: no assets, documents or URLs were supplied, so asset needs are unspecified. A modelled set needs authorized geometry with finished rear and underside surfaces. Reusable glTF parts need inspected node names, pivots and clips. Video-textured screens need authorized footage. A captured turntable needs enough angles. Exporter strings do not establish licensing.
summary.combinations: Explicit: style-078 adds matte clay-like figures that share the set's light rig and contact-shadow softness, while keeping figure-to-architecture scale fixed. Style-024 adds hand-drawn annotations in foreground ink, with at most one accent. Annotations must not cover key models. Avoid mixing glossy and matte finishes, and avoid new accent hues. Use the set alone when the miniature itself is the subject.
summary.productionApproach: Explicit: Blender with Python bpy and Cycles or EEVEE is the style renderer and motion engine for models, materials and offline renders. Optional techniques include toon ramps, geometry outlines, soft lighting and CRT screens; three.js handles browser 3D only if needed. HyperFrames is the default pipeline, with Remotion only under a recorded verified limitation. Template placeholders stay unspecified until the task supplies them.
